Positive bias = optimistic
The model usually predicts more remaining life than actually remains — 69% of endpoints were over-estimated.
Why it matters
Optimistic estimates can delay review. The bias CI (6.47–15.57) lies entirely above zero, so the optimism is systematic.

5 · CONCLUSION
Three conclusions, bounded by clear limits
§6.6, §7.1–7.4, Table 6.1 Backup: provenance ↗ claims boundary ↗
12 / 13
1 · ACCURACY
18.88 cycles MAE
Selected by a frozen PHM tie-break after a near tie; bias +10.90 cycles is optimistic.
2 · UNCERTAINTY
182.46 cycles wide
Whole-engine intervals protected trajectories but were too wide; 63% of lower bounds clipped.
3 · HUMAN REVIEW
39/39 at 81/100 reviewed
All observed high-risk endpoints reviewed, at heavy workload; the prototype kept policy deterministic and the human in charge.
Limits
Secondary simulated FD001 · one regime, one fault mode · 20 calibration engines · stipulated thresholds · no qualified-technician study · no live model-to-workflow link · historical provenance gaps
Not claimed: field effectiveness · validated operational safety · production readiness · aircraft-maintenance certification
Next test
Fresh engine regimes · conditional or group-aware uncertainty · bias correction on new engines · live authenticated interface · qualified reviewers with workload and automation-bias study · immutable provenance
Illustrative turbofan schematic — not a validated engine simulation

Four research questions and their bounded answers

B1
RQQuestionAnswer (§7.2)
RQ1How accurately can lightweight ML models estimate RUL for FD001 under an engine-level, leakage-controlled design, relative to a naive age-only baseline, and which feature groups drive that accuracy?Test MAE 18.88, RMSE 25.73, bias +10.90 cycles; PHM tie-break selected RF despite near-equal validation RMSE vs age alone
RQ2How can engine-block conformal prediction provide RUL intervals with a transparent finite-sample rule, and what coverage–precision trade-off does it create?q̂ 107.90 covered 100/100 endpoints, mean width 182.46; narrower scores covered only 8/20 validation trajectories
RQ3What do SHAP explanations reveal about the selected model, and how can they be read against turbofan physics without being mistaken for causal evidence?Exact reconstruction; age dominant; local core-speed contributions — not physical causes
RQ4How can prediction, uncertainty and explanation be translated into CRITICAL/HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW triage with mandatory human review, and how safe and burdensome is it?Point triage under-triaged 34/100; offline guard caught 39/39 with 81/100 reviews; prototype records three decision types

BACKUP B6 · EQUIVALENCE BAND AND PHM TIE-BREAK
Selection: equivalence band first, asymmetric penalty second
§2.4.2, §4.7, §5.2; PHM score after Saxena et al. (2008a) ↩ Backup index
B6
Rule 1 — practical equivalence
Candidates whose mean engine RMSE lies within 1% of the best are treated as equivalent.
RF 29.479 vs naive 29.556: ratio 1.0026 → within 1%
XGBoost 31.156 and Ridge 31.516: outside the band
Rule 2 — tie-break
Lowest mean PHM penalty among equivalent candidates: RF 83.67 vs naive 156.44.
PHM 2008 penalty, e = predicted − actual
e ≥ 0 (late): exp(e / 10) − 1
e < 0 (early): exp(−e / 13) − 1
Late, optimistic errors are penalised more steeply than early ones.
Ratio 29.556 / 29.479 is derived from Table 5.1. Both rules were fixed before validation results were read.
BACKUP B7 · CONFORMAL SCORE AND RANK
Conformal score: definition, rank and assumptions
§2.5.1, §4.8; Vovk, Gammerman and Shafer (2005); Lei et al. (2018a); Barber et al. (2023) ↩ Backup index
B7
Score
sᵢ = maxₜ |ŷ(i, t) − y(i, t)| for each of n = 20 calibration engines
Rank
Finite-sample rank ⌈(n + 1)(1 − α)⌉ = ⌈21 × 0.90⌉ = 19 → 19th of 20
q̂ = 107.8965 cycles (reported 107.90)
Interval
[max(ŷ − q̂, 0), ŷ + q̂]; clipping changes reported width
Assumptions and caveats
Coverage is marginal under exchangeable calibration and future engines
Not guaranteed per engine, under distribution shift, or as a safety certificate
Calibration covered 19/20 engines by construction — not independent validation
20 engines → coarse order statistic; q̂ sensitive to one engine
